newsitem.title: QATAR: Gulf Air plans second meeting on indebted airline.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air plans second meeting on indebted airline.

text.p: Gulf Air shareholders were unable to reach a decision on Wednesday on ways to improve the $2 billion indebted airline's performance and increase its capital, officials said.
Officials said the shareholders agreed to meet again on Thursday after four-hours of talks during the extraordinary meeting in Doha.
"We had a very good meeting, we discussed a lot of alternatives and it was very enriching," Qatar's Minister of Communications and Transport Sheikh Ahmad bin Nasser al-Thani told reporters.
"We did agree on finalising it at another meeting tomorrow (Thursday) morning."

Bahrain's Transport Ministry Secretary-General for Aviation Affairs Ibrahim al-Hamr earlier told the Qatari news agency the general assembly aimed at increasing the airline's paid up capital by 100 million Bahraini dinars ($297 million).
Airline officials have put the current capital of the airline -- jointly owned by the governments of Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and Abu Dhabi -- at 150 million Bahraini dinars.
Hamr said the company and its board of directors "were intensifying efforts to improve the company's financial position through a lot of rationalisation measures".

The airline's board of directors had approved a "solid financial plan dealing with a number of rationalisation measures covering the airline's stations, fleet and manpower," he added without elaborating.

The board of directors of the Manama-based airline last met in Muscat in November to study measures to shape up the airline which posted $13 million in profits during the 1996 summer season. It suffered a $159 million loss in 1995.
